import MumfordLib.SingularCochains
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Quotient.Defs

/-!
# Generation of integral singular chains

Every integral singular chain is a finite integer linear combination of
simplex generators. We express this as span membership in the morphism space
from the integers, using the coproduct universal property of singular chains.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory

namespace Mumford.Analytic

variable {X : TopCat} {n : ℕ}

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Simplex generators span every integral singular chain. -/
theorem singularChain_mem_span
    (c : ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ (IntegralSingularChainComplex X).X n) :
    c ∈ Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (singularSimplexChain (X := X) (n := n))) := by
  let C := (IntegralSingularChainComplex X).X n
  let E₀ : (ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ C) ≃+ C :=
    ModuleCat.homAddEquiv.trans (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf ℤ ℕ C).toAddEquiv
  let E : (ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ C) ≃ₗ[ℤ] C :=
    E₀.toIntLinearEquiv
  let P := Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (singularSimplexChain (X := X) (n := n)))
  let q := P.mkQ.comp E.symm.toLinearMap
  have hq : ModuleCat.ofHom q = 0 := by
    apply SSet.chainComplex_hom_ext
    intro σ
    apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
    apply LinearMap.ext_ring
    change P.mkQ (E.symm (E (singularSimplexChain σ))) = 0
    rw [E.symm_apply_apply]
    exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero P).mpr
      (Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self σ))
  have hc := congrArg (fun f : C ⟶ ModuleCat.of ℤ ((ModuleCat.of ℤ ℤ ⟶ C) ⧸ P) =>
    f.hom (E c)) hq
  change P.mkQ (E.symm (E c)) = 0 at hc
  rw [E.symm_apply_apply] at hc
  exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero P).mp hc

end Mumford.Analytic
